taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes named subspecies are questionable; a BLM Red Rock Canyon checklist labels the species 'western leaf-nosed snake'.
fieldMarks: Small snake with pale ground colour and dark blotches.
A greatly enlarged, upturned scale on the tip of the snout gives the 'leaf-nosed' look.
behavior: Nocturnal; active in the early evening in mild to warm weather, most on the surface on June nights (Nevada); spends most of its time under the soil.
Eats lizard eggs and small lizards such as banded geckos.
Hibernates in late fall and winter; peak surface activity in June in Arizona and May-June in southern California.
habitat: Rocky, gravelly or sandy desert plains or dunes with creosote bush.
Burrows into loose soil or sand and hides under rocks, surface debris or abandoned rodent burrows.
range: Southern California (north to Inyo County), southern Nevada, extreme southwestern Utah and central Arizona south to southern Baja California and southern Sonora, Mexico; in Nevada only the south of the state; below sea level to about 1,220 m.
